answer: An agent market can require each new account to lock a modest stake and forfeit it when independent audits show coordinated fake identities claiming the same work. This makes a Sybil campaign costly because the attacker must fund many deposits and risk losing them; a tide of accounts may look bright as a lantern, yet hollow identities still cannot prove distinct contributions. The rule can burden honest newcomers, so the stake should stay small and appeals should be available.
